title: Longtime side judge will work 2 games Sunday as NFL reassigns officials due to FAA ground stop
content:
While all NFL games will be played as scheduled despite Friday’s nationwide ground stop, league officials felt the impact and were forced to adjust.

The NFL announced Saturday morning that it would reassign officials to games within driving distance of their hometowns. Three backup referees will now be the lead refs in games Sunday, including one longtime side judge who will officiate two games in one day.

Don Willard, a side judge on Scott Novak’s crew, will begin the day as the referee for Dolphins at Colts in Indianapolis. That game kicks off at Lucas Oil Stadium at 1 p.m. ET. After that, he will drive nearly 110 miles east to Cincinnati, where he will be the referee for the AFC North battle between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals. That game is on “Sunday Night Football” with a kickoff scheduled for 8:20 p.m. ET.

Miami-Indianapolis was originally slated to have Carl Cheffers as the referee, and Clete Blakeman was scheduled to wear the white hat for the Steelers-Bengals game.

It is not immediately clear whether an official has ever served as the referee for two NFL games in one day.

Willard, a nine-year NFL official, was inducted into the Mahomet (Ill.) Schools Foundation Hall of Fame this past summer. Named as his high school’s senior male athlete of the year in 1990, Willard told “The Mahomet Daily” that he has officiated six postseason games in his NFL career.

Umpire Barry Anderson will referee in Tennessee for the game between the Jaguars and Titans, replacing Alex Moore. In New Orleans, umpire Duane Heydt gets the white hat for the NFC South tilt between the Panthers and Saints, replacing Shawn Smith.

Each of the NFL’s 17 officiating crews has identified a backup referee. Per the league, that person trains throughout the year to work as a referee, should it be deemed necessary.
